text: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.
author: Epictetus

archive.text: Mrs. Dalloway said she would buy the flowers herself.
archive.author: Virginia Woolf

archive.text: Know that although in the eternal scheme of things you are small, you are also unique and irreplaceable, as are all your fellow humans everywhere in the world.
archive.author: Margaret Laurence

archive.text: Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.
archive.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

archive.text: A little learning is a dangerous thing.
archive.author: Alexander Pope

archive.text: Before you can inspire with emotion, you must be swamped with it yourself. Before you can move their tears, your own must flow. To convince them, you must yourself believe.
archive.author: Winston Churchill

archive.text: Happiness is the meaning and the purpose of life, the whole aim and end of human existence.
archive.author: Aristotle

archive.text: Don't grieve. Anything you lose comes round in another form.
archive.author: Rumi
